what_happened: The person running Athena deleted the finished producer build folder (10 GB) of job 20261031-111730-dyh4 by hand. This was before the checks stage, when 11 GB was free, just over the 10 GB guard. The job is the b5hm retry, and its earlier attempt had run short of disk in the same stage. No criterion or check had failed. The deletion was done to keep the job from ending failed on low disk. The fix that removes the producer build before checks (hs8s) has not landed.
cause: Athena owns no disk lifecycle. A finished producer's build folder can be regenerated, yet nothing reclaims it or counts it against a disk budget before the checks. The 10 GB guard only reports failure and frees nothing. The fixes (hs8s, and b5hm itself) are ordinary queued jobs that need disk to run. They have not been made urgent, even though this is at least the fifth hand cleanup in two days. Each job near the threshold therefore depends on the person running Athena noticing in time.
prevention: Give Athena a disk lifecycle. Before the checks stage, it should automatically delete the finished producer build folder and any other regenerable artifacts (verify-side builds, caches) once they are no longer needed. If free space is still below the guard, it should hold the job instead of failing it, and resume after space is recovered. Land hs8s and b5hm first, ahead of other work, since they are the fixes for the repeated hand cleanups. Alternatively, run the checks so that they never need the producer build to remain on disk.
proposed_request: Make Athena manage its own disk so jobs no longer need hand cleanup. Outcome: (1) after a producer finishes and before the checks run, Athena removes that job's producer build folder and other regenerable artifacts that are no longer needed (finished baseline or verify-side builds, scratch worktrees), and records what it freed in the job record; (2) if free disk is still under the configured guard after that, the job is held with a clear message and resumes automatically once space is available, rather than ending failed; (3) a hold or low-disk stop is never counted as a failed check or an unmet criterion. Acceptance: a test with a simulated low-disk state shows that the producer build is removed before the checks, that a still-low state produces a hold rather than a failure, and that the job resumes and completes when space returns. Treat this as urgent, and run it ahead of other queued work.
